name: Dana Whitfield
headline: Fractional VP of Sales who turns founder-led services firms into sales-led teams that actually work their inbound

engagements.problem: Inbound leads were going unanswered for days because the founder was still the only closer and nobody owned follow-up.
engagements.what_they_did: Set a 15-minute lead response SLA, hired and trained two account executives, moved the founder out of first calls, and built a simple qualification script in HubSpot.
engagements.outcome: Inbound-to-meeting conversion went from 18% to 46% and the founder stopped taking first calls within 4 months.

engagements.problem: Partners sold ad hoc with no pipeline, so revenue was lumpy and nobody knew what would close.
engagements.what_they_did: Introduced a three-stage pipeline, weekly forecast meeting and the firm's first business development hire.
engagements.outcome: Forecast accuracy within 10% for three straight quarters and 31% revenue growth in year one.

engagements.problem: Bids came in through the website and phone but the owner reviewed every one personally and many went stale.
engagements.what_they_did: Built an estimator-plus-closer team structure, a bid response playbook and a HubSpot workflow for quote follow-up.
engagements.outcome: Average bid turnaround dropped from 9 days to 2 and win rate rose from 22% to 34%.

reviews.quote: Dana got me out of the sales seat without anything falling through the cracks. Our inbound leads finally get a call the same day, and my team closes deals I used to think only I could close.
She is direct, practical and fast. The pipeline meeting she set up is now the most useful hour of our week.
We had tried two sales managers before Dana. She built the process first and then hired against it, which is why it stuck.
Strong operator who knows professional services buyers. I wish we had brought her in a year earlier.

name: Marcus Bell
headline: Fractional VP of Sales for Series A SaaS: builds the first outbound team and the comp plan to go with it

engagements.company: A Series A product-led analytics SaaS company
engagements.problem: Self-serve signups had plateaued and the board wanted an outbound motion, but nobody had ever built one.
engagements.what_they_did: Defined the ICP from product usage data, hired and ramped the first three SDRs and an AE, wrote the outbound sequences in Apollo and designed a comp plan tied to qualified pipeline.
engagements.outcome: $1.9M in new qualified pipeline in the first two quarters; outbound became 35% of new ARR.

engagements.problem: The founders were closing every deal and had no comp structure for their first sales hires.
engagements.what_they_did: Wrote the first sales playbook, built OTE and quota models for AEs and SDRs, and hired the first two reps.
engagements.outcome: First two AEs hit 90% of quota by month six; founder time on sales fell by half.

engagements.company: A $6M edtech platform selling to school districts
engagements.problem: Pipeline depended entirely on conferences and inbound, and there was no repeatable outbound playbook.
engagements.what_they_did: Built an account list by district size, a 14-touch Outreach sequence and a weekly SDR coaching cadence.
engagements.outcome: Meetings booked per month tripled and cost per opportunity fell 40%.

reviews.quote: Marcus built our outbound engine from nothing. The comp plan he designed is still the one we use, and our SDRs actually understand it.
Very strong on hiring and structure. He pushed us hard on ICP definition, which annoyed us at first and paid off later.
He knows how to bolt sales onto a product-led motion without breaking what already works.

name: Priya Desai
headline: Fractional CRO for $20M+ B2B companies: enterprise motion, forecasting discipline and sales leadership hiring

engagements.problem: The CEO was still running the enterprise pipeline and the forecast missed by 30% two quarters in a row.
engagements.what_they_did: Installed MEDDICC qualification, rebuilt the forecast cadence in Salesforce and Gong, and hired a permanent VP of Sales.
engagements.outcome: Forecast accuracy within 5% for three quarters and a successful hand-off to a full-time VP.

engagements.company: A $16M professional services firm selling to hospitals
engagements.problem: Strong inbound demand, but the partners were the only closers and large deals stalled.
engagements.what_they_did: Built a deal desk, a partner-plus-seller selling model and a proposal process for enterprise buyers.
engagements.outcome: Average deal size up 60% and sales cycle shortened by five weeks.

engagements.problem: Two regional sales teams with different processes and no shared forecast.
engagements.what_they_did: Unified the sales process, territory design and weekly forecast across both teams.
engagements.outcome: Unified forecast in one quarter; regional win rates converged at the higher team's level.

reviews.quote: Priya is the best sales leader I have worked with, fractional or full-time. She made our forecast something the board trusts.
She took enterprise deals off my plate and hired the VP who now runs the team. Calm, rigorous and very good with people.
We grew the average deal by more than half while she was here. Worth every dollar.
The rare operator who is equally strong on process and on coaching. Our reps still use her deal reviews.
Excellent, though in high demand, so book her early.

name: Grant Holloway
headline: Turnaround VP of Sales for mid-market companies whose pipeline has dried up

engagements.problem: Pipeline had fallen 45% year over year after two senior reps left and the distributor channel went quiet.
engagements.what_they_did: Re-engaged the top 20 distributors with a joint selling program, restructured territories and put the team on a weekly pipeline review.
engagements.outcome: Pipeline rebuilt to 3.2x coverage in five months and the year closed at 96% of plan.

engagements.problem: Reps were chasing small shippers and margins were collapsing.
engagements.what_they_did: Re-segmented accounts by lane value, changed the pricing guardrails and moved two reps to strategic accounts.
engagements.outcome: Gross margin per load up 18% and average account size up 2.1x.

reviews.quote: Grant walked into a mess and had a plan in two weeks. The distributor program he built saved our year.
Expensive, and blunt with the team, but he knows exactly how to find pipeline when there is none.
Delivered the numbers. Less interested in documenting how so the team could keep it going after he left.

name: Elena Vasquez
headline: Fractional CMO for product-led SaaS: positioning, demand generation and the content engine behind it

engagements.problem: Traffic was growing but trial-to-paid conversion was stuck at 2% and messaging was generic.
engagements.what_they_did: Rewrote positioning around one use case, rebuilt onboarding emails and launched a content program targeting operations managers.
engagements.outcome: Trial-to-paid conversion rose from 2.1% to 3.8% and organic signups grew 70% in two quarters.

engagements.problem: Paid acquisition costs doubled in a year with no clear channel strategy.
engagements.what_they_did: Shifted budget from paid social to partnerships and SEO, and set up channel-level CAC reporting.
engagements.outcome: Blended CAC down 34% while new customers held flat.

reviews.quote: Elena found the one sentence that explains our product. Everything got easier after that, from ads to sales calls.
Smart and data-driven. Needed a bit more support from our side on design resources than we expected.

name: Tom Becker
headline: Fractional CMO for local and regional service businesses: brand, lead generation and reviews

engagements.problem: Phones were quiet outside peak season and the brand looked dated next to competitors.
engagements.what_they_did: Refreshed the brand and website, launched local search ads and a review request program.
engagements.outcome: Off-season call volume up 40% and Google rating from 4.1 to 4.7.

engagements.problem: Relied entirely on referrals and wanted a second source of clients.
engagements.what_they_did: Built a simple website, a legal-guide content series and paid search for two practice areas.
engagements.outcome: Twelve new client matters from search in the first six months.

reviews.quote: Tom gets small businesses. He was practical about our budget and the phones did start ringing.
Good ideas but slow to execute, and we had to chase updates more than I would like.

name: Aisha Okafor
headline: Fractional RevOps leader who makes HubSpot trustworthy before the board meeting

engagements.company: An $11M B2B SaaS company preparing a Series B
engagements.problem: HubSpot had three competing deal pipelines and duplicate companies, so nobody trusted the pipeline numbers going into the board deck.
engagements.what_they_did: Merged pipelines, defined stage exit criteria, deduplicated 14,000 records and built a board dashboard with one definition of pipeline and bookings.
engagements.outcome: Board pack built from HubSpot in under an hour; leadership stopped arguing about the numbers within six weeks.

engagements.problem: Marketing and sales reported different lead numbers and could not agree on what an MQL was.
engagements.what_they_did: Defined lifecycle stages, rebuilt lead scoring and set up a shared funnel report.
engagements.outcome: Single funnel report adopted by both teams; MQL-to-SQL conversion became measurable for the first time (22%).

engagements.problem: Forecasts lived in partner spreadsheets and the CFO had no visibility.
engagements.what_they_did: Moved the forecast into HubSpot with weighted stages and a weekly roll-up.
engagements.outcome: Quarterly forecast within 8% of actual for the first time.

reviews.quote: We had a board meeting in five weeks and a CRM nobody believed. Aisha cleaned it up and gave us numbers I could defend.
She explains RevOps in plain English, which made it easy for our sales and marketing leads to agree on definitions.
Fast, organized and calm. A few dashboards needed tweaks after she left, but the foundation is solid.

name: Ryan Cho
headline: RevOps architect for Salesforce-heavy teams: CRM migrations, territory models and forecasting infrastructure

engagements.problem: Moving from HubSpot to Salesforce with eight years of messy data and a hard cut-over date.
engagements.what_they_did: Designed the Salesforce data model, ran the migration and built the forecasting and territory reports.
engagements.outcome: Migrated on schedule with no lost opportunities; forecast reports live on day one.

engagements.problem: Territories were assigned by hand and reps fought over accounts.
engagements.what_they_did: Built rules-based territory assignment and an account ownership policy in Salesforce.
engagements.outcome: Account disputes dropped to near zero and new-rep ramp time fell by three weeks.

name: Megan Torres
headline: Fractional Sales Enablement leader: onboarding, playbooks and call coaching that get new AEs productive faster

engagements.problem: Two new AEs were taking nine months to close their first deals and there was no written playbook.
engagements.what_they_did: Wrote the sales playbook, built a 30-60-90 onboarding plan with certification checkpoints and ran weekly Gong call reviews.
engagements.outcome: Time to first closed deal fell from nine months to four; both AEs hit 80% of quota in their second quarter.

engagements.problem: Reps ran demos without discovery and win rates were falling.
engagements.what_they_did: Introduced a discovery framework, talk tracks and a call scorecard in Gong.
engagements.outcome: Win rate on qualified opportunities rose from 19% to 28%.

reviews.quote: We did not need another manager, we needed someone to teach our AEs how to sell our product. Megan did exactly that.
The onboarding program she built means our next hires will ramp in half the time. Great with reps.

name: Jordan Blake
headline: Fractional Customer Success leader for agencies and services firms: stop churn, then build expansion

engagements.problem: Clients were leaving after six months and new business barely covered the churn.
engagements.what_they_did: Built a 90-day client onboarding plan, a monthly results review and an account health score, and trained account managers to propose expansions.
engagements.outcome: Logo churn fell from 38% to 19% a year and expansion revenue reached 22% of total.

engagements.problem: Retainers renewed on autopilot with no upsell motion and several large clients quietly shrinking scope.
engagements.what_they_did: Introduced quarterly business reviews, renewal playbooks and an account planning template.
engagements.outcome: Net revenue retention went from 92% to 109%.

reviews.quote: Jordan stopped the bleeding. Our account managers now walk into client meetings with a plan, not an apology.
Practical, agency-savvy and good with clients. The health score was simple enough that we actually use it.
